original_question: Does there exist, in ZFC, a set of reals satisfying Sfin(Omega,Omega) of cardinality d?
target_in_paper: Problem 3.2 in Section 3.1 ("Examples without special set-theoretic hypotheses" / "Dichotomic examples"): "Does there exist (in ZFC) a set of reals satisfying Sfin(Ω, Ω) such that |X| = d?" ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s target problem almost verbatim: it asks for existence in ZFC, concerns a set of reals, uses the same property Sfin(Ω,Ω), and asks for cardinality d. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))
missing_details: Introduce the ambient object explicitly as a set X ⊆ ℝ.
Define Sfin(Ω,Ω) explicitly, rather than leaving it as notation.
Define Ω(X) as the family of open ω-covers of X.

Define an open ω-cover as a nontrivial open cover 𝒰 of X such that every finite F ⊆ X is contained in some U ∈ 𝒰; in the paper, “cover” is understood to be nontrivial, i.e. X itself is not a member of the cover.
Spell out 𝔡 as the dominating number.

If you want the question to reflect the paper’s exact motivation, mention that the issue is whether the critical cardinality 𝔡 for Sfin(Ω,Ω) can be realized in ZFC, since the paper notes only a ZFC example of size cf(𝔡) from dichotomic arguments.
refined_question: Working in ZFC, does there exist a set of reals X ⊆ ℝ with |X| = 𝔡, where 𝔡 is the dominating number (the least cardinality of a family D ⊆ ω^ω such that for every f ∈ ω^ω there is g ∈ D with f(n) ≤ g(n) for all but finitely many n), such that X satisfies Sfin(Ω,Ω); that is, for every sequence ⟨𝒰_n : n ∈ ℕ⟩ of open ω-covers of X, there exist finite subfamilies 𝔽_n ⊆ 𝒰_n such that ⋃_{n∈ℕ} 𝔽_n is again an open ω-cover of X, where an open ω-cover means a nontrivial open cover 𝒰 of X with the property that every finite F ⊆ X is contained in some U ∈ 𝒰? ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))
justification: The draft targets Problem 3.2 exactly, not a broader neighboring question. Section 1 supplies the meanings of Sfin(A,B), ω-cover, and Ω, and Section 3.1 then states the question verbatim as Problem 3.2. The surrounding paragraph explains why this is the sharp formulation in the paper: dichotomic ZFC arguments already yield a set of reals satisfying Sfin(Ω,Ω) of size cf(d), while the critical cardinality recorded for failure of Sfin(Ω,Ω) is d, so the unresolved issue is whether the exact critical cardinal d can be attained. The next item, Problem 3.3, is different: it asks for a direct non-dichotomic construction of a set satisfying Sfin(Ω,Ω) but not Ufin(O,Γ). The later Problem 10.6 is a group-theoretic analogue and is also different from the target here. ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDgt/Pearl%20E.%20%28ed.%29%20Open%20Problems%20in%20Topology%20II%20%28Elsevier%2C%202007%29%28ISBN%200444522085%29%28723s%29_MDgt_.pdf))
